summary: Cast-iron light at the north entrance to Bonne Bay, first lit in 1898 after an 1889 campaign; three keepers, the last retiring in 1970; now part of a Gros Morne exhibit.

structures.type: two-storey wooden house, connected to the tower by a covered way

access.note: Site open; keeper's house open daily mid May to mid October (2026: 15 May to 12 October); tower closed.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Coast Guard's current list gives Iso W 4s, which is used. Wikidata (record) gives Fl W 4s, and Rowlett describes a white flash every four seconds. These describe the rhythm in different terms; the current official list is kept.

notes_for_editor: 1) Ownership conflict: LF says the Canadian Coast Guard owns the lighthouse and that the keeper's dwelling passed to Parks Canada when a lease expired; Rowlett says ownership of the lighthouse passed to Parks Canada in 2014. Both are in the story. The record's 'Parks Canada' agency follows Rowlett. 2) Date conflict: the record and Rowlett date the station 1897; LF says the iron tower was ordered in 1893, the lantern arrived in 1894, and the light was not lit until spring 1898. The story gives both. 3) The Parks Canada 2026 page says visitors can 'step inside our century old lighthouse' for the exhibit; LF and Rowlett put the exhibit in the keeper's house. The story says keeper's house per LF and Rowlett; the tower is closed in all three. 4) Characteristic: Iso W 4s (CCG current), Fl W 4s (Wikidata, record), white flash every 4 s (Rowlett). 5) LF cites the Journal of the House of Assembly of Newfoundland for its Nevill-era details. That journal was not read here. Fearn's words come second-hand through LF; the story quotes one sentence of them, as LF prints it (checked 2026-10-27). 6) LF spells Bonne Bay as Boone Bay once; the story uses Bonne Bay. 7) Privacy: the 1970 tenant is named in LF as an artist; the story says only 'a private tenant' and the evidence list keeps the name internal. R. L. Hynes is a contractor and is not named in the story. George Young is named only in his keeper and flag-raising roles, as LF prints them; LF's family details (eight children) are omitted. 8) No DMF corpus hits (Newfoundland joined Canada only in 1949), no newspaper search, and the Chance Heritage Trust page was not read; the story rests on LF, the register, Rowlett, Parks Canada and the CCG list.
